subject: DPA: scope of processor obligations, edge cache handling, and onshore fallback
body:
From: procurement@medsecure.com
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@medsecure.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA redlines and question about edge caching

Hi Olga / Kimberly,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA earlier. We reviewed and attached redlines—there are a couple of items where we need clear confirmation from Redwood before we can proceed:

1) Service provider vs processor language: we want explicit language confirming Redwood is a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA and will not sell the data.
2) Edge cache and CDN behavior: our security team is concerned about transient copies of telemetry/requests leaving the US. Can you confirm the geographic limits on edge caching or an onshore fallback?
3) Subprocessor notice timing: request 30 days prior notice and the right to object for certain categories.

Attached: MedSecure_DPA_redlines_20270502.pdf

We also included a simplified dataflow diagram in case that helps.

Regards,
Marta Gomez
Procurement | MedSecure
[Attachment: MedSecure_DPA_redlines_20270502.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]
[Attachment: dataflow-diagram-v2.png (PNG, 128KB)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <procurement@medsecure.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and question about edge caching

Marta — thanks for the redlines and diagram. Appreciate the clear asks. Quick notes up front while Kimberly and Aditya dig in:

- Redwood confirms: we operate as a service provider/processor (we call it "service provider" in our US addenda) and do not sell customer data. We'll add explicit language that matches your wording.
- Edge caching: we have a policy that allows short-lived caching at regional POPs to optimize latency; however, we can commit to an onshore-only fallback for telemetry/identifiers for customers in scope if that is required contractually. I asked Aditya for the specifics on TTLs and eviction behavior.
- Subprocessor notice: we typically provide 30 days notice for material subprocessor changes and immediate notice for security-critical additions. Kimberly will propose the legal wording.

I'll loop back with a consolidated reply and suggested language.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Privacy Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <procurement@medsecure.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and question about edge caching

Hi Marta — attached I'm sending a marked-up section we think will satisfy MedSecure's requirements and keeps the clause operationally enforceable. High-level:

- Processor/Service provider language: proposed text mirrors CPRA guidance — Redwood will be a "service provider" and will not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information for any purpose other than for the business purposes described in the Agreement. We added an explicit "no sale" representation.
- Onshore fallback & edge cache carve-out: new paragraph that requires Redwood to use geographically restricted caching for customer-identifying telemetry when the customer selects the "US-only" option. If that option is selected, Redwood will route requests away from non-US POPs for any identifiers flagged as enterprise telemetry.
- Subprocessor notice: we accepted 30 days for non-critical subprocessors and immediate notice for security-sensitive subprocessors (e.g., log storage, identity providers). We kept an objection window of 15 days.

We did not accept a blanket right to approve subcontractors (too operationally restrictive), but we can offer a process for expedited substitution or privileged review for high-risk categories.

Proposed language attached in the PDF. Let us know which specific paragraphs MedSecure would like tightened.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_proposed_clauses_20270503.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <procurement@medsecure.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and question about edge caching

Marta — adding technical context so the legal wording maps to how the runtime behaves. Highlights below and a short checklist for MedSecure's engineering/security team.

1) Edge caching behavior:
- We perform short-lived prefix caching and KV cache at regional POPs to reduce tail latency. Typical TTLs are sub-60s for generative request prefixes and sub-300s for telemetry aggregates.
- Caches do not persist model context beyond the session; KV caches are ephemeral and evicted on session termination.

2) Onshore fallback option:
- If MedSecure elects the US-only telemetry option, requests carrying enterprise-identifiers will be routed to US-region serving pools. We will disable routing to EU/APAC POPs for those request types.
- This fallback does not apply to third-party CDN origin pulls for static assets; if MedSecure needs full control, we recommend the dedicated/private deployment option.

3) Subprocessor and log storage:
- We use an encrypted log storage provider (onshore or sovereign deployments dependent on purchase) and can provide evidence of encryption-in-transit and at-rest.

Checklist for MedSecure (technical):
- Confirm you want "US-only telemetry" (yes/no)
- List any categories of data you consider "sensitive telemetry" that require stricter TTLs or immediate eviction
- Confirm whether you need a dedicated/private deployment for full onshore residency

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the dataflow diagram.

– Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Will Hutchins <will@privacyconsults.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marta Gomez <procurement@medsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and question about edge caching

Folks — quick third‑party note from the compliance review side. A few pragmatic suggestions that typically speed signoff for healthcare customers:

- Add an explicit "telemetry classification" appendix that lists identifiers considered personal vs aggregated telemetry, and tie eviction TTLs to those classes (e.g., PII-tagged logs < 30s).
- For subprocessor objections, add a predefined remediation path (e.g., substitution within 30 days and data migration assurances) rather than an open approval right. This reduces legal back-and-forth while protecting the customer.
- Include a compact evidence package link (SOC2 summary + encryption attestations + sample log retention config). Customers appreciate a single link instead of multiple PDFs.

I can draft the appendix language and a remediation flow if helpful.

Best,
Will Hutchins
Principal, PrivacyConsults

From: procurement@medsecure.com <procurement@medsecure.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Will Hutchins <will@privacyconsults.io>, legal@medsecure.com
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and question about edge caching

Thanks all — this is helpful. MedSecure can accept the proposed service provider language and the 30/15 day notice/objection cadence for subprocessors. We do want the US-only telemetry option and would like the telemetry appendix Will mentioned.

Next steps:
- Kimberly/Olga: please prepare a short appendix draft for telemetry classification + eviction TTLs and add the onshore fallback language we discussed.
- Aditya: please confirm the exact TTL values for PII-tagged logs vs aggregated metrics and whether the onshore routing is switchable without a redeploy.
- Will: if you can draft the appendix text, we can iterate quickly.

If we can close those three items by EOD Friday (05/07), procurement will circulate the final DPA for signature.

Regards,
Marta Gomez
Procurement | MedSecure
